text: Sandboxes are isolated, programmatically managed runtime environments for running code
quote: Sandboxes are isolated runtime environments you can manage programmatically to run code.

text: Snapshots capture point-in-time sandbox state including filesystem, packages, dependencies and settings
quote: Snapshots are persistent, point-in-time captures of sandbox state, including the filesystem, installed packages, dependencies, and settings.

text: GPU sandboxes offer NVIDIA GPU acceleration for inference, fine-tuning, and CUDA workloads
quote: GPU sandboxes with NVIDIA GPU acceleration for model inference, fine-tuning, and CUDA-accelerated compute.

text: Volumes are FUSE-based mounts providing shared file access across sandboxes
quote: Volumes are FUSE-based mounts that provide shared file access across Daytona sandboxes.

text: MCP server can be initialized with AI agents like Claude, Cursor, and Windsurf
quote: Initialize the MCP server with your preferred AI agent. Supported agents include Claude, Cursor, and Windsurf.

text: Supports stateful Python execution in a persistent interpreter carrying variables/imports across runs
quote: Run independent code snippets where each execution starts from a clean interpreter state... run Python code in a persistent interpreter context with variables, imports, and state to carry across executions

text: Computer Use provides mouse, keyboard, screenshot, recording, and display control for GUI automation in sandboxes
quote: Computer Use enables programmatic control of desktop environments within sandboxes. It provides mouse, keyboard, screenshot, screen recording, and display operations for automating GUI interactions and testing desktop applications.

text: Firewall parameters can be set at sandbox creation or updated live to control network access
quote: Set firewall parameters when creating a sandbox or update them while the sandbox is running.

text: Browser-based web terminal lets users run commands and debug sandboxes without local tools
quote: Daytona provides a browser-based web terminal for interacting with your sandboxes. The web terminal allows you to run commands, view files, and debug directly from your browser without installing any local tools.

text: Official TypeScript SDK for programmatic sandbox interaction
quote: The Daytona TypeScript SDK provides a powerful interface for programmatically interacting with Daytona Sandboxes.

text: Official Python SDK for programmatic sandbox interaction
quote: The Daytona Python SDK provides a robust interface for programmatically interacting with Daytona Sandboxes.

text: Official CLI provides command-line access to sandbox lifecycle, snapshots, and more
quote: Daytona provides command-line access to core features for interacting with Daytona Sandboxes, including managing their lifecycle, snapshots, and more.

text: Windows OS runtime available in a VM for running Windows applications and tooling
quote: Windows OS runtime in a virtual machine for running Windows applications and tooling.

text: Sandboxes can be spun up and shut down in milliseconds, used only as needed
quote: Daytona lets you spin up sandboxes in milliseconds and shut them down just as fast. Use what you need, when you need it.

text: VM sandboxes with dedicated Linux or Windows operating systems are available
quote: Daytona also provides VM sandboxes with a dedicated Linux VM or Windows operating system

text: MCP server enables AI agents to programmatically interact with Daytona sandboxes
quote: Daytona Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI agents to interact with Daytona Sandboxes programmatically.

text: Code execution supports multiple languages with both stateless and stateful persistent-context modes
quote: You can run code snippets in multiple languages with support for both stateless execution and stateful interpretation with persistent contexts.

text: Custom sandbox images/Dockerfiles can define OS, runtimes, packages, and setup, built into snapshots
quote: define the base operating system, language runtimes, packages, and project-level setup in an image or Dockerfile, and Daytona builds it into a snapshot you can use to create sandboxes

text: Snapshots persist filesystem state (cold) or filesystem+memory state (hot) depending on sandbox type
quote: captures and persists a sandbox’s current state; container sandboxes capture filesystem state only (cold snapshots), VM sandboxes capture filesystem and memory state (hot snapshots)

text: Warm pools keep pre-created running sandboxes from a snapshot for instant claim on matching requests
quote: keep a configured number of pre-created, running sandboxes built from a snapshot; matching sandbox create requests claim one warm sandbox from the pool instantly instead of provisioning a new sandbox

text: Volumes let sandboxes instantly read large files without manual upload to each sandbox
quote: They enable sandboxes to read from large files instantly - no need to upload files manually to each sandbox.

text: Firewalled sandbox network prevents untrusted code from exfiltrating data or reaching arbitrary hosts
quote: Each sandbox runs behind a firewall that restricts which external IP addresses and domains it can reach, preventing untrusted code from exfiltrating data or contacting arbitrary hosts.

text: Free tier includes $200 in compute credits to start building without contacting sales
quote: Use what you need, when you need it. $200 in free compute included.

text: Project remains public, free to use, fork, and build on under its license
quote: It remains public and free to use, fork, and build on under the LICENSE, as is and without support or warranty.
